title: Blast Column
pages: Shape four clay balls around iron bars into a Green Tuyere, then fire it in the fuel-fired Kiln at 600 degrees for 180 ticks. The Ceramic Tuyere survives the furnace blast; the green body or loose bricks cannot replace it in the Blast Column controller craft. Craft the controller from four sealed steel plates, two magma blocks, two bricks, a blast furnace and this fired tuyere. Its tuyere channels the bosh air; the structure's four iron-bar sides represent the external air inlets. The Kiln is available before the Blast Column. It is a 3x3 blast furnace stack six courses tall (43 blocks plus the controller). Build it from the bottom up. Course 1, the hearth, is a blast furnace two blocks below the controller, ringed by eight stone bricks. Course 2, the bosh, is a magma block on top of the furnace with an iron-bar air inlet on each of its four sides and stone bricks in the corners. Course 3 holds the controller with a brick pillar in each corner; its four sides stay open so you can reach the controller. Course 4, the shaft, is a full ring of eight bricks around a source lava block placed directly above the controller; the ring keeps the lava from spreading. Course 5, the heat-recovery throat, has four brick sides and four copper-block corner sinks, leaving the center open. Course 6, the exhaust cap, has four iron-bar side vents; its center and corners remain open. The copper sinks sit above the shaft corners and the vents sit above the throat bricks. A Structure Projector bound to the controller shows each course in turn. Every block must stay in place. A stone brick in place of a brick stops the column.

Right-click the formed controller with four matching items to run one column_blasting batch. Four amethyst shards vitrify into one amethyst insert for the Resonance Infuser. Sand, cobblestone, clay balls and netherrack also produce useful construction materials. Removing any hearth, tuyere, pillar, shaft, copper sink or exhaust vent, the magma, the furnace or the source lava stops processing without consuming items.

Stone-variant batches smooth and polish quarried blocks at scale: stone, sandstone, red sandstone, quartz block and basalt each fire into their smooth form, while andesite, diorite, granite and blackstone polish directly. Cobbled deepslate fires into deepslate and red sand vitrifies into glass alongside ordinary sand. The shared heat returns five blocks per batch of four for netherrack, smooth stone, smooth quartz, smooth basalt, the four polished stones and red-sand glass. Sand, cobblestone, clay, sandstone, red sandstone and cobbled deepslate stay four for four because crushers, mills or quench vats turn their products back.

Specialty batches recover materials the furnace cannot: a full clay block fires into terracotta (distinct from the clay-ball-to-brick batch), wet sponges dry out, soul sand compacts into soul soil, and eight gravel fracture under heat into two flint shards.

The column uses arcana_industry:column_blasting datapack recipes exclusively; ordinary minecraft:blasting recipes do not run here. For manual use, the structure consumes only the held batch and drops output if the inventory is full. For automation, insert stock through the top or horizontal controller faces with a hopper or item pipe. The formed column runs one batch every 40 ticks and buffers products for extraction from the bottom. Sneak-use an empty hand on a face to cycle input, output and disabled; use an empty hand normally to collect buffered products. The stock and output buffers persist across saves. The column has no FE port.
